newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana grants 12 coffee buying licences.
newsitem.headline: Ghana grants 12 coffee buying licences.

text.p: Ghana's Cocoa Marketing Board (COCOBOD) granted provisional licences to 12 private companies to buy and export coffee beans, coffee products, sheanuts and sheabutter.

The announcement, in a COCOBOD statement, follows press reports from the Brong Ahafo Region that farmers are threatening to cut down coffee bushes and plant corn because they find no buyers for a stock of 12,000 bags of coffee.
Ghana, a small producer of low-grade coffee, exported 1,400 tonnes of coffee, coffee husks and skins in the first nine months of 1996, according to Ghana Customs statistics.
Since 1991, the World Bank has been trying to boost the sector but industry sources say results have proved disappointing.
The project includes importation and development of new varieties as well as distribution of planting material to smallholders.
Annual production, estimated at less than 10,000 tonnes, was partially smuggled to Ivory Coast, a local World Bank agriculturalist told Reuters last year.
